runners_data.name: Onslow Gardens
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist whose recent form on Standard going reads poorly (9/15, 0W2P sim-going) and who has drifted out to 10f recently, making this mile drop back feel like it needs a strong pace to suit — Alec Voikhansky has limited opportunities here and this profile is hard to trust at the top of the betting.|

runners_data.name: Mount Mogan
runners_data.note: Thorough Standard-going performer (14/15, 3W5P) who drops back to his best distance range of 7-8f and has Laura Mongan in fine trainer form; Georgia Dobie takes the ride for a yard that rarely runs without purpose, and this nine-year-old has shown he retains his form cycle.|

runners_data.name: Manton Road
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse by inclination — his last five runs all show late-finishing patterns — but the bunched midfield means he will struggle to find his usual berth; Callum Hutchinson rides, and there is a noteworthy STYLE_FIT concern (0.92) as racing without his customary cover reduces his winning prospects.|

runners_data.name: Whitesnake
runners_data.note: Jason Watson partner who has raced mainly at six and seven furlongs in sharper company, stepping up to a mile here; his Standard-going exposure is thin (2/5) and while he is a natural closer, the redistribution into midfield means he is unlikely to get the sectional he needs — Watson's quality helps but the trip is unproven.|

runners_data.name: Withoutfurtherado
runners_data.note: Dougie Costello is a positive booking, but this horse's sim-going record is stark (2/15, 0W0P on Standard) and he has run over 10f most recently, suggesting stamina is more his game than a one-mile tactical affair; being shuffled out of his preferred rear position by a crowded hold-up contingent compounds the concern.|

runners_data.name: Ocean Force
runners_data.note: David Probert has significant claims in the jockey market but Ocean Force has run just four times, all without a win or place on Standard going (1/4), and the 63-day absence adds uncertainty; Gary and Josh Moore are a live yard (T14: 4/23) and this horse has the profile of one needing a strong pace that is unlikely to materialise.|

runners_data.name: Nubough
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old who is supremely course-and-distance wise — all 15 recent runs on Standard, 2W5P — and Kieran O'Neill knows him well; he comes back off a 91-day break (headgear flagged: t) and that layoff after a modest recent run is the one reservation on what is otherwise the most proven course performer in the race.|

runners_data.name: Warrnambool
runners_data.note: Returned just nine days ago and that quick turnaround is worth noting; Ryan Kavanagh (3lb claim) partners this natural closer who has a visor entry, but the horse's Standard-going sim record (10/15, 0W1P) and lack of a win in five starts make this a difficult win case even before accounting for the midfield redistribution.|

runners_data.name: Bajan Bandit
runners_data.note: The confirmed front-runner who will dictate the fractions — Paddy Bradley takes the ride and this horse has placed at Lingfield at 8f on Standard before (2nd, 1W6P sim-going); STYLE_FIT is flagged at 0.93 because he is a pure leader mapped slightly away from his natural role in the data, but in practice he is most likely to secure the front and control the race.|

runners_data.name: Dandy Khan
runners_data.note: Pat Cosgrave is a top-quality booking for Jim Boyle and this four-year-old has a strong Standard-going record (13/15, 3W7P) — he consistently races at 7f but steps to a mile, which is an untested distance for him; his hold-up style is genuine and he will need to find a clean path from the pack, though his consistency gives him live claims.|

runners_data.name: Muy Muy Loco
runners_data.note: Tyler Heard partners a horse who won over 10f on Standard and has strong Lingfield AW form (12/15, 2W5P) — the drop back to a mile is the key question after several runs at 10-11f, and the 155-day absence is a notable flag alongside the headgear (h); Simon Dow has a 1/8 T14 return suggesting the yard is ticking over.|

runners_data.name: Francisco
runners_data.note: Patrick Chamings runner who won at 7f on Standard last time (8/15 sim-going, 1W4P) and returns just seven days later — the headgear combination (tv) and Alfie Redman's 7lb claim could help at the weights, but a fourth consecutive run without a break and a step up from 7f to a mile here are concerns for this hold-up type.|

races.paceDynamic: Bajan Bandit is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner Lingfield AW mile handicap and, with no genuine rival likely to chase him hard from the break, he should be able to dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop from his prominent berth. The pace is unlikely to be strong enough to string the field out early, which means the race will be run at a rhythm that suits those travelling comfortably in the first half-dozen, rather than those needing a truly searching test to reel in the leader. Withoutfurtherado, Ocean Force, Whitesnake, Warrnambool and Manton Road are all natural hold-up types redistributed into midfield positions because this field genuinely holds more rear-of-field horses than the map can accommodate at the back — of those, Dandy Khan and Mount Mogan are best placed to secure closer-to-pace berths, but several will be racing without the cover they prefer. The race shape overwhelmingly favours horses who can travel prominently and be produced with a single run from two furlongs out — prominent racers and the very sharpest off a moderate pace are the profiles to side with; true closers who need a strong tempo to close off will be left wanting.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Bajan Bandit Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Bajan Bandit bowls along at a comfortable clip and no rival has the pace or inclination to pressurise him through the first half-mile.
scenarios.body: Bajan Bandit sets a moderate, uncontested gallop from the front and, with a clear lead turning in, his handler Pat Morris's record of placing him fresh is relevant at just 13 days since his last run; the field will concertina into him approaching the straight, suiting horses who can quicken off a moderate pace rather than those needing strong fractions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Mount Mogan or Dandy Khan track Bajan Bandit in the first two or three and quicken past him in the straight without needing a deep finish.
scenarios.body: Mount Mogan's strong Standard-going record (14/15 runs, 3 wins, 5 places) and class at seven and eight furlongs make him the most credible challenger to the leader, while Dandy Khan's consistency at Lingfield on Standard gives him solid claims if he can get a position just off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Bajan Bandit sets a surprisingly strong early pace or the pack bunches and a fast-finishing hold-up horse threads through in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires a pace injection that is not guaranteed given Bajan Bandit's profile and the absence of a second true front-runner; Manton Road is the most credible beneficiary if he can get a clear run from the rear, given his 1W4P record in similar going and a recent course win, but he is racing out of his natural position which tempers confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaotic Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution of multiple hold-up types into the midfield causes traffic problems and the race develops into a rough, bunched finish with no clean run for the favoured profiles.
scenarios.body: With five genuinely redistribued hold-up horses crammed into the midfield, a falsely run race could produce scrimmaging in the straight that scrambles the outcome; Francisco (7lb claimer Alfie Redman aboard, headgear, course winner at 7f) or Muy Muy Loco could each benefit if a gap appears at the right moment, though both face questions about the step back up in distance.

watchPoints.text: Bajan Bandit's early position is the race-shaping key — if Paddy Bradley allows him to bowl along unchallenged from the gate, the moderate pace he sets will dramatically compress the field turning in and expose horses racing out of their preferred hold-up roles.

Mount Mogan's draw and early position are critical — Georgia Dobie must place him close enough to Bajan Bandit to pounce in the straight, as his Standard-going record makes him the most dangerous legitimate challenger to the leader if he gets the right tactical ride.

The five redistributed hold-up horses (Withoutfurtherado, Ocean Force, Whitesnake, Warrnambool, Manton Road) crammed into midfield create a genuine traffic-risk scenario approaching two furlongs out — watch for interference as any or all seek a run simultaneously.

Nubough's 91-day layoff needs careful monitoring in the early market moves — if he is backed from his morning price it suggests the yard believes the break has freshened him for this course and distance where he is the most proven competitor in the field.

Dandy Khan steps up from his habitual 7f trip to a mile for the first time in his recent pattern — if Pat Cosgrave opts to ride him closer to the pace than usual to compensate for the longer trip, it would signal that connections believe the mile suits, and that tactical shift is worth watching in the early stages.

races.name: Follow @attheraces On X Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Gunfighter
runners_data.note: Seven-furlong form at Lingfield AW is solid (1W2P sim-going) but Pat Dobbs rides a horse that wants to come from off the pace; squeezed into midfield by the volume of closers in this field, its natural late kick may be blunted before the straight arrives.

runners_data.name: Sant Alessio
runners_data.note: Front-runner likely to dispute the lead aggressively with Double Time; returned after 50 days and trainer Joe Tickle has a modest 14-day strike rate, but Standard going and a confirmed front-running style keeps it squarely on the map.

runners_data.name: State Of Madness
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane in good recent form (2/14); prominent runner with eight runs on sim-going returning 1W4P, and three of his last five over 7f — sits in the ideal position if the pace plays out truly.

runners_data.name: Double Time
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old confirmed front-runner wearing headgear, last won over 8f on Standard — the drop to 7f could catch him out in a finish but he'll be a genuine pace-setter regardless; Tim Vaughan sends just one runner in the 14-day window, low-key angle.

runners_data.name: Dontspoilasale
runners_data.note: Tom Queally rides a prominent-style horse with 13 runs on sim-going (2W2P) but recent form reads all 6s and 7s; needs something to go wrong ahead of it to win, though it will at least be in the right part of the track.

runners_data.name: Starlight Sami
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type with the best recent form in the book — won over 7f Good and placed on Standard, George Bass claiming allowance helps the weight; if traffic clears in the straight this is a live each-way profile.

runners_data.name: Split Elevens
runners_data.note: Best course specialist in the field: 13/15 on sim-going, 3W8P, recent win over this exact trip and track (1/7f/STA); prominent style means it should slot in cleanly behind the duelling leaders and is the most in-form visible runner.

runners_data.name: Yachtsman
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type wearing tongue-tie, winning form over 6f Good but limited Standard-going experience (3 runs, 0W1P); step up to 7f is unproven, Jason Watson has to produce him wide late if this works at all.

runners_data.name: Powder Monkey
runners_data.note: George Boughey has 4/22 14-day runners which is active; prominent runner returning after 89 days — that layoff is the main concern, though two places over 7f AW (0W2P on sim) suggest the track and trip suit if fitness is there.

runners_data.name: Paranjape
runners_data.note: Apprentice Millie Wonnacott (5lb claim) provides a useful weight relief; prominent style with a place over 6f Standard, but headgear (p) and 46-day absence mean this needs luck in running from a busy prominent group.

runners_data.name: Red Hat Eagle
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who keeps hitting the frame on Standard (7 runs, 1W3P sim-going) — Taylor Fisher and William Knight combine quietly; headgear (tp) suggests the horse needs anchoring and may settle better with a genuine pace to chase.

runners_data.name: Bold Suitor
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with phenomenal Standard-going record: 15/15 runs, 3W9P — no going concern whatsoever; prominent style, recent win at this trip (1/7f/STA), and Georgia Dobie's claim; the course-and-distance form is the standout stat.

runners_data.name: The Bitter Moose
runners_data.note: David Probert takes the ride on a hold-up type wearing a visor (first time?); 59-day break and only 3/15 on sim-going (0W1P) makes this an outsider profile — needs a very specific set of circumstances that this shape is unlikely to produce.

runners_data.name: Dancing Rinca
runners_data.note: Hayley Burton's 7-year-old has only two visible recent runs on 6f Good going, which is shorter and different surface from today's requirements; bumped to midfield by the cluster of closers, its true hold-up style is further compromised by limited Standard-going evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Sant Alessio and Double Time are confirmed front-runners who will contest the lead from the off over Lingfield's 7f Polytrack, creating a genuinely contested pace rather than a lone leader controlling tempo. Six of the fourteen runners want prominent positions, producing a congested early shuffle that makes clean passage between the 2f and 3f poles a real concern — runners like State Of Madness, Dontspoilasale, Split Elevens, Powder Monkey, Paranjape and Bold Suitor will all be pushing for the same real estate. The field holds more hold-up types than the rear of the race can accommodate; Gunfighter and Dancing Rinca are genuine closers but are effectively displaced into midfield by the volume of hold-up traffic, meaning their late runs may be compromised. This shape — honest pace from two leaders, prominent bunch jostling — sets up best for horses positioned just off the pace in a genuine midfield berth, able to travel into the race as the front two tire in the final quarter-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Sant Alessio and Double Time fight for the lead and set an honest gallop that burns off true hold-up runners late.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners press each other through the first three furlongs, creating a genuine pace that softens the principals and hands the initiative to horses travelling smoothly just off the pace; the final two furlongs on Lingfield's straight Polytrack reward those who can sustain a run from a prominent berth without having battled for early position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Steals
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner secures an uncontested lead early and the prominent pack fails to apply sustained pressure.
scenarios.body: Double Time or Sant Alessio blinks first and cedes lead without a fight, allowing the other to control a falsely steady gallop that rewards front-end stamina over staying power; at 7f on a flat Polytrack a leader who dictates their own fractions can hold off a non-threatening pack if prominent horses are caught in traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Hold-Ups Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes interference or checking between 2f-3f out, creating a gap for late closers.
scenarios.body: The bunching of six prominent types in a 14-runner field creates a wall that blocks midfield runners momentarily, opening a clear route for the few genuine hold-up horses who find daylight late; Lingfield's straight final furlong rewards sustained finishing kicks, but this scenario is partially undermined by the fact that several nominal closers are redistributed and not operating in their true role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Ups Claim But Compromised
scenarios.trigger: If redistributed closers Gunfighter and Dancing Rinca find a clear run from midfield despite racing out of their natural role.
scenarios.body: Neither horse is operating in its true hold-up position and both carry STYLE_FIT discounts, so this outcome requires the race to develop in an unusually chaotic fashion that creates a wide-open straight; the scenario is assigned low probability precisely because both horses are tagged as racing out of role and their finishing kicks may not materialise as effectively from a midfield rather than rear berth.

watchPoints.text: Split Elevens has won twice over this exact course and trip on Standard going and sits in the ideal prominent position — watch whether it can slot cleanly behind the two leaders and make a sustained challenge from 2f out.

Bold Suitor's 15/15 Standard-going record is remarkable and a 9/10 in-the-money rate demands respect — watch Georgia Dobie for an attempt to sit just off the prominent bunch and time a run in the straight.

The double front-runner scenario (Sant Alessio vs Double Time) risks either burning them both out or causing one to capitulate early and hand a soft lead — watch the first furlong closely to see which shape materialises.

Six prominent-style runners chasing the same two or three positions creates real traffic danger between 2f and 3f out — any horse forced wide or checked in that corridor loses ground it cannot afford to give back at this trip.

Gunfighter and Dancing Rinca are genuine hold-up types mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear — watch whether Pat Dobbs or Kieran O'Neill can find clear running in the straight or whether their finishing kicks arrive too late from an unnatural position.

races.name: Sky Sports Racing Virgin 512 Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Dark Mandate
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's hold-up 3yo hasn't run in 302 days — the layoff is a significant concern, and with only 2 placed efforts from 7 starts on similar going and no win in this surface type, she needs everything to go right to feature.|

runners_data.name: Solar Phoenix
runners_data.note: Roger Teal runner with a genuine hold-up profile but pushed forward in the mapping because the rear is oversubscribed; racing out of his optimal position and with only one placing from five runs on similar going, the fitness edge of a 13-day return is partly offset by a likely awkward race.|

runners_data.name: Pennine Way
runners_data.note: One of three confirmed front-runners who will battle for the lead from the off; his recent form shows a 3rd and 2nd on Lingfield-equivalent standard going but finishing 7th last time out at Goodwood suggests he needs the pace to suit rather than be too fierce.|

runners_data.name: Mister Moet
runners_data.note: The most accomplished of the front-runners with 2 wins and 5 places from 15 similar-going runs — his AW record is the standout of the pace trio, and with Kieran O'Neill aboard he may be best equipped to manage a hot early pace without burning all reserves.|

runners_data.name: King Cherry
runners_data.note: Third confirmed front-runner but his form figures of 75867 and zero wins or places from 5 similar-going runs makes him the least likely of the pace trio to convert; his presence is significant for pace-making purposes but his win claims are weak.|

runners_data.name: Lieutenant Sir
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's 3yo won impressively over 6f on good ground at Goodwood and has ability, but his natural hold-up style means this hot-pace race may force him forward of his comfort zone — Watson's 0 from 22 over the last 14 days is a minor concern.|

runners_data.name: Fuseboard
runners_data.note: Chelsea Banham's horse boasts a win at 5f on standard going and a place from 6 similar-ground runs, and while he is a genuine hold-up type, the congested rear means he will likely race further forward than ideal — the 44-day absence adds mild fitness doubt.|

runners_data.name: Apex Star
runners_data.note: William Knight's prominent racer has a solid profile for this race shape — five runs on similar going with two places and a record of tracking the pace — and Taylor Fisher keeps the ride; well-suited if the front-runners do the expected damage to each other.|

runners_data.name: Reality Queen
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's highest-rated runner in the field at OR-60 and a winner over this trip, though her four runs on similar AW going show zero wins or places; she needs the pace to collapse fully to get involved from her hold-up position.|

runners_data.name: Royal County Glory
runners_data.note: Jack Jones's 3yo is a genuine prominent racer with a win over 7f on standard going and four places from 11 similar-going runs — her profile of sitting just off the pace suits this race shape well, and the 80-day break is the only modest concern.|

runners_data.name: Mayfair Market
runners_data.note: Millie Wonnacott (5lb claim) takes the ride for S Woods, but form figures of 5-6897 and zero wins or places from four similar-going runs make her hard to trust; the hold-up style also means she needs the stars to align in this pace-heavy contest.|

runners_data.name: Love Alive
runners_data.note: David Probert partners John Butler's hold-up type who has shown ability at this trip, with a win from 13 similar-going runs; the 15-day return is positive freshness and she is one of the more interesting deep closers if the front-runners truly combust.|

races.paceDynamic: Pennine Way, Mister Moet, and King Cherry are all confirmed front-runners and will contest the early lead aggressively from the gates, guaranteeing a strong, unrelenting gallop over this 6f Lingfield AW surface. With three horses fighting for the same territory, fractions will be quick and the pace is unlikely to ease mid-race, meaning stamina will be tested throughout and the race is likely to be run in a manner that strings the field out early. The hold-up brigade — Dark Mandate, Reality Queen, Mayfair Market, and Love Alive — face a legitimate opportunity to close late if the pace burns out the leaders, but the field contains more hold-up types than can all settle cleanly at the rear. Solar Phoenix, Lieutenant Sir, and Fuseboard are genuine hold-up horses who are mapped to midfield but will likely find themselves racing closer than ideal given the volume of pace ahead; of the three, Lieutenant Sir's recent Goodwood win from a prominent position suggests he may adapt best, while Solar Phoenix and Fuseboard are less likely to benefit from a shape they cannot fully exploit. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape heavily favours prominent-to-midfield closers with proven stamina at 6f on AW — horses who can sit just off the hot pace and pick up the pieces as the three front-runners potentially tie each other up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Pennine Way, Mister Moet, and King Cherry burn each other out setting a genuine strong gallop, the race sets up for the best-credentialed midfield closers.
scenarios.body: The three leaders drain each other's reserves through a fast first three furlongs, leaving the race wide open in the final furlong for horses tracking the pace or closing from genuine midfield; Apex Star and Royal County Glory are ideally positioned as prominent types who can sit just off the battle and pounce. Love Alive and Reality Queen also have live claims if they can close from deeper positions before the wire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Frontrunner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three lead-contenders — most likely Mister Moet given his two wins and strong AW form — manages to edge clear of the others and control the pace without burning out.
scenarios.body: Mister Moet's 12 runs on similar going with 2 wins and 5 places suggests he handles this surface best of the pace trio and could find a rhythm if the others fade back; if he gets a comfortable lead he is capable of kicking clear before closers can organise. Pennine Way is the alternative beneficiary if he gets first run off the bend and the others do not match him stride for stride.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Deep Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is even more fierce than expected and all three front-runners capitulate in the final furlong, hold-up horses get a rare opportunity to sweep through.
scenarios.body: Reality Queen's OR-60 and win record on AW-adjacent conditions, and Dark Mandate's hold-up profile both come alive in this scenario if they can get a clean run through tired horses; Love Alive also fits this shape given her hold-up style and creditable recent form. The risk is that the closers are numerous and may block each other's runs in a condensed finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Steadies, Front Runs Clear
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders reach a tacit understanding and the gallop is steadier than the pre-race picture suggests, allowing the lead trio to conserve energy and sprint clear.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely scenario given three genuinely aggressive pace-pusher profiles, but if it materialises Mister Moet and King Cherry — both with headgear entries — are best placed to hold on as the field fails to close; Royal County Glory's prominent style means she could also track a steadier pace and prove dangerous. The hold-up horses would be comprehensively disadvantaged in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Pennine Way, Mister Moet, and King Cherry will clash for the lead immediately — watch the first two furlongs for which, if any, gets a clear advantage, as the one who settles in front without a prolonged fight has a materially improved chance of lasting.

Mister Moet's AW record (2W, 5P from 15 similar-going runs) makes him the stand-out of the pace trio — if he gets a clean break from the stalls and avoids being dragged into a frantic duel, he becomes a significant threat to hold on.

Royal County Glory and Apex Star are prominent types who should be able to sit just behind the pace battle — watch where they settle in the first furlong, as a clean position behind the lead duel puts both in the ideal shape-beneficiary spot.

Dark Mandate's 302-day layoff is the longest absence in the field — watch for any signs of ring-rustiness in the parade ring or early in the race, as a hold-up horse returning from near a year off needs everything to go perfectly.

Lieutenant Sir, Solar Phoenix, and Fuseboard are all natural hold-up types likely to be pushed forward by the race shape — watch how each jockey handles the opening stages, as those who can resist and drop in may still get a meaningful late run.|

races.name: Download The At The Races App Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Queen Sana
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with three runner-up finishes in her last four starts, all at 5-6f on Good or Firm — the drop to Standard AW is untested but Jason Watson claiming the ride for Ollie Sangster (2 from 19 in 14 days) adds confidence she's fit and ready.

runners_data.name: Fiorella Princess
runners_data.note: 134-day absence is the significant concern here, though Robert Cowell's horses often return fit and her five places from fifteen AW starts on Standard going show she handles this surface well; headgear worn previously and front-end style should see her land a prominent pitch from Charles Bishop.

runners_data.name: Sea Her Excel
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner in the field and capable of dictating entirely — her sole AW start produced a win on Standard at this trip and Elle-May Croot's 5lb claim keeps the weight manageable; all recent wins came on Good, so the surface switch is the only query but the evidence points in her favour.

runners_data.name: La Belle Forest
runners_data.note: Won at 5f on Standard AW and holds strong course form, but her natural hold-up style means she will likely find herself racing closer to the pace than ideal in this race shape — Archie Watson (0 from 22 in 14 days) is a minor negative and 63 days off the track adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Whizzy Dizzy
runners_data.note: Seven runs without a win and a string of mid-pack finishes (4th, 4th, 6th, 7th) suggest a horse that finds little when asked — Georgia Dobie rides and Clive Cox is in good form (6/22 in 14 days), but the pattern of form offers little encouragement for any scenario.

runners_data.name: Little Jaybee
runners_data.note: Returned to form with back-to-back thirds on Good just 8 days ago, so fitness is not the concern — however, her true hold-up style is squeezed forward by this race shape, meaning Pat Cosgrave cannot ride her to her strengths, and that redistribution materially dampens her prospects.

runners_data.name: Over Spiced
runners_data.note: Remarkably consistent, placing in five of her last six starts at 5f on Good for Grace Harris, with David Probert retaining the ride — headgear noted and a 14-day turnaround for a stable with 2/19 in the same window; everything about her profile suits a prominent-run race on a fast, straight 5f.

runners_data.name: Independent Expert
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist whose recent form includes a 9th, 8th, and 6th over 6-7f on Good — stepping down in trip marginally helps, but Tom Queally needs pace to collapse in front and this race shape makes that an unlikely gift.

races.paceDynamic: Sea Her Excel is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should stride into an uncontested position from the gates, setting a sustainable gallop over this straight Lingfield 5f on Standard ground. Queen Sana, Fiorella Princess, and Over Spiced will push forward to dispute the prominent berths behind her, creating a defined early order but not enough sustained pressure to destabilise Sea Her Excel's rhythm. This field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — La Belle Forest and Little Jaybee, both true hold-up horses, are likely to find themselves racing closer to the pace than their natural style dictates, compromising the late kick they depend upon. The dominant race shape favours a front-runner who can control fractions unchallenged and the prominent horses who can travel just behind without being burned off — patient closers face an uphill task on a straight 5f where ground is rarely given back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Lead Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Her Excel goes unchallenged to the front and controls a moderate, even tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: Sea Her Excel sets the fractions to suit herself and, with no rival willing or able to go with her, simply maintains momentum to the line without ever being headed. Prominent horses Queen Sana and Over Spiced, travelling just behind in a rhythm rather than fighting for position, are best-placed to pick up any gaps but may find the leader has too much in reserve.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Her Excel's lead is soft enough that the prominent trio travel comfortably and produce a finishing burst in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Queen Sana and Over Spiced, both consistent placers at this trip, utilise their prominent positions to swoop past a tiring leader inside the final furlong, with the even gallop having played perfectly into their hands. Over Spiced's solid recent form (four consecutive top-three finishes on Good) and Queen Sana's repeated placing at 5f suggest both have the class to capitalise if the front-runner wavers.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine enough to soften the prominent runners and a closer finds a gap on the rail in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: La Belle Forest, a winner at this course and distance on Standard, would be the most likely beneficiary if the pace stretches the field and a seam opens late — though her redistribution to midfield means she is unlikely to be in her natural position. Fiorella Princess, with five places from fifteen runs on similar going, could also finish powerfully if traffic clears, but both scenarios depend on a faster early tempo that the current race shape does not guarantee.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Overhauls Itself
scenarios.trigger: If Queen Sana or Over Spiced push aggressively early and the pace proves self-defeating, leaving all prominent types vulnerable to a late finisher.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop would burn off the prominent types and give the genuine hold-up runners a chance to come from further back, though Whizzy Dizzy and Independent Expert have shown inconsistency at this trip and neither has demonstrated a reliable late turn of foot on this surface. This remains the least likely shape given the clear pace hierarchy and the redistribution of the true closers away from their optimal positions.

watchPoints.text: Sea Her Excel is the only confirmed front-runner — if she misses the break or is taken on early by Queen Sana or Over Spiced, the entire race shape unravels and hold-up types gain a fighting chance.

La Belle Forest and Little Jaybee are true hold-up horses likely to race closer to the pace than ideal — watch whether Cosgrave and Cox allow them to drop in naturally or are forced forward, as their draw position will be telling at the off.

Over Spiced's recent string of near-misses (five places, no wins) raises the question of whether she can convert — if she travels prominently into the final furlong without finding, the race opens to Sea Her Excel's stamina.

Fiorella Princess returns from a 134-day break — Robert Cowell's AW sprinters often run well first time back, but any signs of ring rustiness at the start or in the early furlongs should be noted for next time.

Whizzy Dizzy (Clive Cox, 6/22 in 14 days) is worth monitoring in the market — Cox is in a rich vein of form and if the stable has sharpened her up from her recent flat performances, she could outrun a bigger price than expected.
